steps.title: Draw one edge
steps.instruction: Draw the left edge of the slice and press Run.
steps.explain: goto(x, y) chooses a position on the grid. Negative x is left of center; negative y is below center. The pen is down for the slanted edge.
steps.expected: One golden line from the upper left to the bottom tip.
steps.question: Which coordinate controls how low the tip goes?
steps.answer: The second input, −145, is its vertical position.

steps.title: Add the other edge
steps.instruction: Draw from the tip to the upper right.
steps.explain: The two top corners use opposite x-coordinates and the same y-coordinate. This gives the slice matching sides.
steps.expected: A V-shaped outline.
steps.question: Why do both top corners use y = 80?
steps.answer: They are at the same height.

steps.title: Close the triangle
steps.instruction: Join the right corner back to the starting point.
steps.explain: The third movement closes the outline. Trace the three points in order before running.
steps.expected: A closed triangle.
steps.question: What would happen if the last point were (0, 0)?
steps.answer: The last edge would end in the middle of the slice, leaving the outline open.

steps.title: Fill the base
steps.instruction: Insert begin_fill() before the triangle movements and end_fill() after them.
steps.explain: The outline already works. These two commands fill the area enclosed by that outline, using the current color.
steps.expected: A solid golden triangle.
steps.question: Which commands have to be between begin_fill() and end_fill()?
steps.answer: The movements that trace the shape.

steps.title: Add the cheese
steps.instruction: Draw a smaller, lighter triangle inside the first one.
steps.explain: Shapes drawn later cover earlier shapes. This smaller triangle leaves a golden border visible around the cheese.
steps.expected: Pale cheese with a golden edge.
steps.question: Why is the cheese drawn after the base?
steps.answer: Its lighter fill needs to sit on top of the base.

steps.title: Make one pepperoni
steps.instruction: Use two filled circles at the same position.
steps.explain: dot() takes the circle’s diameter. The smaller red circle sits inside the larger dark circle, leaving a rim.
steps.expected: One pepperoni with a darker edge.
steps.question: Which number controls the outside diameter?
steps.answer: 47. The second dot, with diameter 37, covers its center.

steps.question: Which two numbers would a reusable pepperoni function need?

steps.question: Which command changes thickness without moving the crust?

steps.instruction: Use two matching arcs to enclose a small leaf.
steps.explain: Each circle(13, 70) draws part of a circle. The turn between them points the second arc back toward the starting point.
steps.expected: A green leaf between the top pepperoni.
steps.question: What does 70 control in circle(13, 70)?
steps.answer: How many degrees of the circle are drawn.

steps.title: Repeat the tested leaf
steps.instruction: Put the working leaf code in a loop with three positions.
steps.explain: setheading(30) resets the direction for each leaf. Without that reset, the turns from one leaf would affect the next.
steps.expected: Three basil leaves and a complete pizza slice.
steps.question: Why reset the heading inside the loop?
steps.answer: Each leaf should start facing the same direction, regardless of where the previous leaf finished.
